title: New methods to color the vertices of a graph
key_finding: Describes heuristic vertex-colouring methods based on comparing vertex degrees and graph structure (the DSATUR approach); one method is exact for bipartite graphs. Also gives an exact method reported to outperform the Randall-Brown algorithm and colour larger graphs, and compares the new heuristics with classical and exact methods.
limitations: Abstract gives no instance sizes or quantitative results; 1979 original.
algorithm: DSATUR (saturation-degree greedy) and DSATUR-based exact backtracking
notes: All candidate fields confirmed by OpenAlex (pub. date 1979-04-01). OpenAlex abstract reconstruction was partly garbled in its last sentence. OA: bronze (ACM PDF).

title: An upper bound for the chromatic number of a graph and its application to timetabling problems
key_finding: Links the basic timetabling/scheduling problem to vertex colouring of a graph (no two adjacent vertices share a colour, minimum colours). Gives a colouring algorithm and a new, easily computed upper bound on the chromatic number in terms of vertex degrees.
limitations: Two-page note; no computational evaluation reported in the abstract.
algorithm: Welsh-Powell (largest-degree-first greedy) colouring and degree-based upper bound
notes: Metadata confirmed. DISCREPANCY IN INDEXES: OpenAlex and Crossref list only D. J. A. Welsh as author; the OUP article page lists D. J. A. Welsh and M. B. Powell, so both are kept. Not open access.

title: A graph coloring algorithm for large scheduling problems
venue: Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards
key_finding: Presents a new graph colouring algorithm (RLF) and compares it with many known algorithms. It shows O(n^2) time on most sparse graphs and is suited to large scheduling problems. Also gives a generator of large random test graphs with known chromatic number, used to evaluate the algorithms.
limitations: Evaluation on generated random graphs, per the abstract.
algorithm: Recursive Largest First (RLF)
notes: OpenAlex and Crossref record only the first page (489). The full range 489-506 is confirmed by the PubMed Central record. OpenAlex lists the DOI landing page as bronze OA.

title: Smallest-last ordering and clustering and graph coloring algorithms
key_finding: Uses smallest-last vertex ordering and priority search to find all connected subgraphs that are maximal with respect to minimum degree, in O(|E|+|V|) time and 2|E| space. Notes that smallest-last graph colouring can be implemented in O(|E|+|V|) time and discusses useful properties of the colourings it produces.
limitations: Theoretical/algorithmic; abstract reports no empirical benchmark.
algorithm: Smallest-last (degeneracy) ordering for greedy colouring
notes: All candidate fields confirmed by OpenAlex (1983-07-01). OA: bronze (ACM PDF).

title: Reducibility among combinatorial problems
venue: Complexity of Computer Computations (eds. R. E. Miller, J. W. Thatcher, J. D. Bohlinger, as listed by Springer), Springer, Boston, MA
key_finding: Encodes problems on graphs, sets, integers and Boolean formulas as language-recognition problems, treating a problem as satisfactorily solved by a polynomial-time algorithm. Shows that many classic unsolved covering, matching, packing, routing, assignment and sequencing problems are equivalent: either all have polynomial-bounded algorithms or none does.
limitations: Theoretical complexity result; no algorithms or experiments.
algorithm: NP-completeness reductions (includes chromatic number / graph colouring)
notes: OpenAlex: book chapter, 1972, pp. 85-103, no abstract. Abstract and editors taken from the Springer chapter page. Springer lists three editors (Miller, Thatcher, Bohlinger) and 'Springer, Boston, MA'. The candidate named no editors. The original print publisher was not confirmed in retrieved sources.

title: Linear degree extractors and the inapproximability of max clique and chromatic number
key_finding: Derandomises the Håstad and Feige-Kilian results, showing that approximating MAX CLIQUE and CHROMATIC NUMBER within n^(1-epsilon) is NP-hard. Also derandomises Khot's quasi-polynomial-time hardness result, using a new disperser construction related to randomness extractors.
limitations: Pure complexity theory; no algorithms for practical colouring.
algorithm: Inapproximability of chromatic number
notes: Confirmed by OpenAlex and the journal page (vol. 3, article 6, pp. 103-128). OpenAlex gives issue '1', but the journal numbers by article, so issue is null. OA: diamond.

venue: Texts in Computer Science, Springer Cham (Springer Nature Switzerland AG)
key_finding: Publisher description: a textbook treating graph colouring as an algorithmic problem with an emphasis on practical applications. It describes and analyses well-known colouring heuristics, covers complexity, bounds and constructive algorithms, and applies them to seating plans, sports scheduling and university timetabling, with downloadable C++ code. The author's site lists code for Greedy, Welsh-Powell, DSatur, Greedy-IS, RLF, Backtracking DSatur, TabuCol, PartialCol, Hybrid EA, AntCol and hill climbing.

key_finding: Solves the independent-set formulation of graph colouring by column generation, solving the LP at each branch-and-bound node implicitly. limitations: Effective for small-to-moderate problem sizes, per the abstract.

title: An introduction of preference based stepping ahead firefly algorithm for the uncapacitated examination timetabling
key_finding: A discrete firefly algorithm for uncapacitated exam timetabling. It builds the initial solution by reordering exams and slots with a heuristic ordering, and uses neighbourhood searches with a preference-based 'stepping ahead' mechanism. It reports results comparable to the best in the literature on the 12 Toronto instances. The full text describes Largest Degree (LD) ordering, which sorts exams by number of conflicts, as one of the graph heuristics.
limitations: Uncapacitated (Toronto) formulation only; no handling of post-publication changes.

title: Solving the list coloring problem through a branch-and-price algorithm
key_finding: Presents a branch-and-price algorithm for weighted list colouring based on a stable-set vertex-cover formulation, with theory on indistinguishable colours. Extensive experiments show the approach is effective.
